summary.text: 说 means “speak” or “say.” It is the standardized simplified form corresponding to 説, a variant of traditional 說. In the traditional graph, 言 marks the speech-related meaning and 兌 is identified as the sound element.

formation.text: The traditional graph 說 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 言 supplies the speech-related meaning and 兌 supplies a sound cue. The simplified graph 说 retains the sound-side shape 兑 and uses 讠, the standardized simplified left-side form of 言. The dossier does not establish that 兌 also contributes meaning.

components.text: 讠 is the left-side simplified form of 言, the speech-related semantic element in traditional 說. The 1986 standard identifies 讠 as a simplified radical and lists 说〔説〕; this supports its simplified-form relation here.

兑 is the visible simplified form of traditional 兌, identified as the sound element in 說. The dossier reports no usable current reading for 兌 and no independently verified same-system historical comparison; the sound role is supported by the traditional analysis.

sound_limitation.text: The dossier supplies no current Mandarin reading for 兌 and no independently verified same-system reading pair for 兌 and 說. The attested historical analysis identifies 兌 as phonetic, but the available evidence here does not permit a sound comparison.

history.text: The traditional analysis names 言 and 兌 in 說 and identifies 兌 as phonetic; the Shuowen gloss is “to explain or release,” with a second gloss relating to discussion. These are historical lexicographic interpretations, not proof of the graph’s earliest origin or sense. The curated seal-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact, and does not establish a sequence of forms.

The standardized list gives 说〔説〕 and treats 讠 as the simplified left-side form used for 言. The dossier also records 説 as a variant of 說. These graphic relationships do not establish when the forms first arose.

The earliest graphic attestation remains unresolved: no primary dated manuscript or inscription image was verified. The proposed Warring States Chu forms are secondary reports in this dossier, not a confirmed earliest sequence.

uncertainties.text: The documented construction supports 言 as semantic and 兌 as phonetic, but the dossier does not establish a historical sound comparison independently or support a semantic contribution from 兌. A historical commentator’s additional semantic interpretation remains an interpretation.

The earliest attested use of the spoken senses and their chronology are unresolved. The dictionary records uses including discussion, explanation, reporting, admonishing, persuasion, and joy, but its citations do not establish the earliest occurrence or a sequence of semantic developments.

Proposed word-family and Proto-Sino-Tibetan explanations for the traditional character’s readings are competing hypotheses; this dossier does not adjudicate them or establish a semantic path among the senses.

senses.text: The dossier records “speak, say, talk” for 说 and the traditional graph. No securely dated earliest occurrence is established, so this is not labeled the earliest attested sense.
The traditional dictionary account records explanation and discussion uses. It does not establish their chronological relationship to “speak” or “say.”
Admonishing and persuasion are recorded uses of the traditional graph; their chronology relative to other senses is not established here.
The merged record includes “scold” and “upbraid” among the character’s glosses. The dossier gives no chronology or supported development from another sense.

limitations.text: The dossier does not establish a dated earliest occurrence or a supported semantic sequence among speaking, explaining, discussing, admonishing, persuasion, and scolding.

overview.text: 说 means “speak” or “say.” It is the standardized simplified counterpart of 説, a variant of 說; the traditional graph pairs a speech-related element with a sound element.

components.text: 讠 is the simplified left-side form of 言, the speech-related part of the traditional graph.
兑 corresponds to traditional 兌, identified as the sound part in 說.

relationships.text: In 说, 讠 is the simplified left-side form of 言, which marks the speech-related meaning in the traditional graph 說.
兑 corresponds to traditional 兌, identified as the phonetic element in 說. The dossier supports that analysis but supplies no verified sound pair for an independent comparison.
The standardized list gives 说〔説〕 and identifies 讠 as a simplified radical used for 言.
The traditional dictionary records 説 as a variant form of 說.
